title: DPA Addendum — Private Deployment & Vendor Security Assessment (DRAFT)
content:
Purpose:
This document is a working DPA addendum and vendor security assessment checklist intended for use when Redwood Inference ("Redwood") provides Private Deployments (VPC/on-prem packages) or when customers operate Redwood-managed components within their environment. It is a draft template meant to be negotiated with legal counsel and technical owners.

Status: DRAFT — internal review only. Do not send to customers without legal sign-off.

-- OVERVIEW / SCOPE --
Applies to: Any customer or vendor engagement that involves processing of Customer Personal Data, Confidential Business Data, or regulated data types (PII, PHI, financial data) within Private Deployments, including (but not limited to) VPC-hosted instances, dedicated GPU pools located in customer-controlled networks, and on-premise/air-gapped installations.

Key objectives:
- Define roles (Controller/Processor) and responsibilities for Private Deployments.
- Capture minimum technical and organizational security controls required for onboarding and continued operation.
- Define breach/incident response, audit rights, and data lifecycle obligations (return/deletion).

-- DEFINITIONS (short-hand) --
Customer Data: Data provided by or collected on behalf of the Customer that is processed by Redwood in connection with the Services.
Personal Data: Any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person.
Subprocessor: Any third-party engaged by Redwood to process Customer Data on behalf of the Customer.
Private Deployment: Any instance of Redwood software or managed components that run within customer-managed networks or dedicated hardware, including VPC workflow and on-prem packages.

-- DRAFT CLAUSES --
1. Roles and Purpose
1.1 Parties acknowledge Customer is the Data Controller and Redwood is the Data Processor with respect to Personal Data processed under this Addendum, unless otherwise agreed in writing.
1.2 Processing Instructions: Redwood shall only process Customer Data in accordance with documented instructions from the Customer, the Agreement, and this Addendum. Any changes to processing instructions require written approval.

2. Security and Minimum Controls
2.1 Redwood warrants it will maintain technical and organizational measures appropriate to the risk, including the controls listed in Appendix A (Minimum Controls).
2.2 Where Redwood operates components within the Customer environment (e.g., a managed agent, telemetry shard, or support access tooling), Redwood will: 
  - Limit access to named personnel and service accounts;
  - Use mutual TLS or equivalent for all inbound/outbound control plane connections;
  - Encrypt secrets at rest using customer-managed KMS when requested (note: implementation options vary for air-gapped installs).
2.3 Customer retains the right to require alternate controls where regulatory obligations demand higher assurances; such requests will be evaluated in good faith and may affect commercial terms.

3. Subprocessors and Third Parties
3.1 Redwood shall provide a current list of Subprocessors upon request and notify Customer of material changes.
3.2 Customer may object to a new Subprocessor on reasonable security/privacy grounds; parties shall attempt resolution within 30 days.

4. Data Transfers
4.1 For transfers outside the EEA/UK (or other applicable jurisdiction), Redwood will rely on standard contractual protections, appropriate transfer mechanisms, or obtain Customer consent as required.

5. Audit, Certification, and Assessments
5.1 Customer (or an independent auditor appointed by Customer) may, subject to agreed scope and confidentiality, audit Redwood's compliance with the Addendum once per 12 months or following a material security incident. Audits must be conducted during normal business hours and with at least 30 days' notice.
5.2 Redwood will provide evidence of independent assessments (SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001, or equivalent) where available. For Private Deployments, Redwood will provide architecture diagrams, control mappings, and a completed Vendor Security Assessment (VSA) checklist (Appendix B) as part of onboarding.

6. Incident Response and Notification
6.1 Redwood will notify Customer without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours upon becoming aware of a confirmed data breach affecting Customer Personal Data processed by Redwood. Notification will include: summary of the incident, affected data categories, remediation steps taken, and recommended Customer actions.
6.2 For Private Deployments where Customer operates the environment, Redwood's notification timeline may be adjusted based on mutually agreed operational playbooks; Redwood will still provide timely technical details to enable Customer remediation.

7. Data Retention, Return, and Deletion
7.1 Upon termination or expiry, Redwood shall, at Customer's choice, return Customer Data or securely delete it within 60 days unless retention is required by law. For on-prem/air-gapped installs, deletion procedures must be verified by Customer with documented proof (hashes, wipe logs).

8. Liability and Indemnity (placeholder — legal to finalize)
8.1 Drafting note: negotiate cap on liability, carve-outs for wilful misconduct, and insurance requirements (e.g., cyber liability).

9. Confidentiality
9.1 Each party shall treat the other party's Confidential Information with at least the same degree of care as its own, and restrict disclosure to need-to-know personnel and authorised advisors.

10. Termination and Suspension
10.1 Customer may suspend processing or demand secure isolation if Redwood materially breaches the Addendum and fails to remediate within a reasonable cure period. Operational impacts and rollback plans must be coordinated with Redwood SRE/Support.

-- Appendix A: Minimum Controls (working checklist) --
A1. Identity & Access
  - Role-based access controls for Redwood personnel; documented approval workflow for escalation.
  - MFA required for all privileged accounts.
A2. Network & Transport
  - All control-plane communications mutually authenticated (mTLS).
  - Support access requires ephemeral credentials and just-in-time access with audit logs.
A3. Data Protection
  - Encryption at rest for persistent token stores; customer-managed KMS option for keys.
  - In-transit encryption for all data planes.
A4. Logging & Monitoring
  - Retention policy for audit logs (configurable per contract).
  - Alerting for anomalous access patterns to model serving endpoints and control plane.
A5. Hardening & Patching
  - Published baseline images with CVE management process; critical patches applied within defined SLA.
A6. Backups & Recovery
  - Encrypted backups; documented restore drills annually for customer-impacting components.

-- Appendix B: Vendor Security Assessment (VSA) Checklist (summary) --
This checklist is intended to be completed by Redwood infra/product engineering during customer onboarding. Items marked "(optional)" may be requested by Customer for high-risk regulated workloads.
1) Architecture diagram with network segmentation labels.
2) List of all third‑party libraries and runtime dependencies used in the deployed package, including versions.
3) Evidence of secure defaults (CSPs, TLS configs).
4) SOC2/ISO certificate links or summary of scope.
5) Pen test summary (last 12 months) and remediation plan.
6) Data flow map identifying where Personal Data is stored/processed and any transient caches (e.g., KV cache).
7) Support access process and escalation contacts.
8) Disaster recovery RTO/RPO targets and recent test results.
9) Cryptographic algorithms and key rotation policy.
10) Known limitations / features planned that may impact data residency or isolation.
